# upwind_access_scope (Resource)

Manages an Upwind access-management scope: a named filter defining a slice of resources.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An access-management scope is a named filter selecting a slice of resources.
#
# The values must name cloud accounts your organization has onboarded.
resource "upwind_access_scope" "production_aws" {
  name        = "Production AWS"
  description = "Resources in the production AWS accounts"

  resource_filters = [
    {
      attribute = "cloud_account_id"
      operator  = "in"
      values    = ["123456789012", "210987654321"]
    }
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Scope name.
- `resource_filters` (Attributes Set) Filters defining which resources fall in this scope. Unordered (a set). (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--resource_filters))

### Optional

- `description` (String) Scope description.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) ISO8601 timestamp when the scope was created.
- `creator_id` (String) ID of the user who created this scope.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for this scope (server-generated).
- `update_time` (String) ISO8601 timestamp when the scope was last updated.

<a id="nestedatt--resource_filters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `resource_filters`

Required:

- `attribute` (String) Resource attribute the filter applies to.
- `operator` (String) Filter operator applied to `values`. `in` matches resources whose `attribute` equals any of the given values.
- `values` (Set of String) Values to match against. Unordered (a set).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import upwind_access_scope.production_aws uams-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```
